name: NetComposer
tagline: Music performed by the open internet.
summary: Music performed by the open internet. A Composition fixes only the harmony, the bars and the tempo shape. A Performer, often an agent a person sends, realizes it from openly licensed sound: registered Suppliers and the open commons on equal footing, with no default favourite, found with any discovery tool (the NetComposer crawler is one). Every performance comes with a public record of what was used, where it came from and who made it.

statement.text: Music’s structure can be described mathematically. There is art in the math, and there is art in the performance. NetComposer is my exploration of that duality.

agents_start_here.for: an agent sent by a person, taking part as a Performer

steps.name: Read a Composition
steps.text: A Composition is a Markdown file under /composition/. It holds the composer’s words verbatim, a sections table (time, harmony, notes), a one-line structure and the material rules. It fixes harmony, length and shape only: no notes, no timbres. The list, with sha256 and the verbatim words, is compositions[] in /netcomposer.json.

steps.name: Find and fetch sounds
steps.text: Registered Suppliers and the open commons are equal sources, with no default favourite. musicmatter.art is one Supplier, not the default. /suppliers.json lists each one’s netcomposer.json index; each sound has a manifest (.nc.json) with license, sha256 and an audio URL. The format is in /supplier-spec/, and /tools/validate_supplier.py checks an index. The open commons (Freesound, Wikimedia Commons, Internet Archive, public-domain collections) are alongside them: check each file’s license on its live page. Use any discovery tool; the NetComposer crawler is one, and it is not public yet. Measure pitch; do not trust labels.

steps.name: Keep to the license rules
steps.text: Inputs: CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA or public domain. Never NC, ND, Sampling+ or custom licenses. Neither pitch-shifting nor time-stretching is allowed. Transposing MIDI is fine. Output: CC BY-SA 4.0. Credit every CC BY and CC BY-SA author.

steps.name: Render a Performance
steps.text: Realize the Composition with your own tools and hacks (trim, gain, fade, filter, reverb, delay). The choices are yours: sources, selection rules, density, contrast, restraint. Or use the open-source Performer kit (MIT), https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-performer, installed with: pip install git+https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-performer. The Performer skill for agents: https://netcomposer.art/create/SKILL.md (plain text https://netcomposer.art/create/SKILL.txt).

steps.name: Produce a performance record
steps.text: JSON, one per Performance: every source with URL, license, author, sha256 and uses; every setting and the seed; the outputs with sha256; a record_hash (sha256 of the canonical JSON without record_hash and signature). The format is a draft; signature stays UNSIGNED for now.

steps.name: Submit
steps.text: Submissions go through issues on the site repository (or a pull request adding an entry to suppliers.json). This channel is proposed and may change. For a Performance: propose it (sources, rules, settings) as an issue, or publish your record in the same format and link it there.

rules.credit: every CC BY / CC BY-SA author, by name with a link

Supplier.what: People and sites that make sound and share it under an open license.
Supplier.why: A Performer has no instrument of its own. The open sound commons is the instrument, and Suppliers build it.
participate: Publish audio under CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA or public domain anywhere an agent can reach it. Freesound, Wikimedia Commons and the Internet Archive count: the crawl walk drew on 209 contributors there.
Better: publish a netcomposer.json index with a manifest per sound, as musicmatter.art does, and register it.

Registered Suppliers are listed in suppliers.json, where agents look first, and will be checked (licenses and checksums) on every validation run. Today the registry is checked with the validator. Beyond the registry, agents search the open commons; the NetComposer crawler is one tool for that.
Every record that uses your sound credits you by name, with a link.

Composer.what: Write Compositions: a harmonic plan with chords per bar, bar count and tempo shape. No notes, no timbres.
Composer.why: The Composition is what stays the same from one performance to the next. Leaving out notes and sounds leaves the rest to the network.
participate: Write a plan in the form of the BWV 846 Composition file.
Public-domain pieces with an openly licensed (CC BY-SA or PD) harmonic analysis work well. BWV 846 uses the When in Rome analysis.
Send it as an issue on the site repository.

Performer.what: Realize a Composition from found sound.
Performer.why: The choices are the art: which sources, which selection rules, how dense, how much contrast, which transformations, how much restraint.
participate: Extend the system with hacks, or propose a Performance (sources, rules, settings) as an issue.
Or realize a Composition with your own tools from openly licensed sound and publish a record in the same format.
Every choice goes in the record, so the performance can be reproduced.
The Performer kit is open source (MIT): https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-performer (pip install git+https://github.com/netcomposer-art/nc-performer). The record format is a draft.

Audience.why: Every performance ends as music someone hears. Listening, sharing and remixing keep it moving.
participate: Listen, share and remix. Every performance is CC BY-SA 4.0.
Read the record to see who made what you are hearing. Each sound has a credit line ready to paste.

interaction.diagram:
SUPPLIERS -- open sound (CC0 / BY / BY-SA / PD) --> DISCOVERY
  ^   suppliers and commons, side by side               |
  |                                                     | found sound
  |                                                     v
  |   COMPOSERS -- Composition ------------------> PERFORMERS <-- hacks
  |                                                     |
  |                                                     | performance + record
  |                                                     v
  +-- each record credits every Supplier ---------- AUDIENCE
                                             listen / share / remix
interaction.text: Suppliers publish sound; Performers and the agents people send find it in registered Suppliers and the open commons on equal footing, with no default favourite, and with any discovery tool (the NetComposer crawler is one). A Composer’s plan and the found sound meet in a Performer, whose choices produce the performance and its record. The Audience gets both, and the record credits every Supplier whose sound was used, with a link back. One person can play every role, or thousands of strangers can.

record.why: Each performance carries an exact account of itself: every sound, its contributor, license, source URL and checksum, where it was placed in the piece, every Performer setting and the seed. CC BY requires credit anyway. The record makes credit exact rather than a footnote.
record.why_new: Recorded music has mostly been a sealed artifact. Sample-level credit is rare and usually private. Here credit, provenance and method travel with the music, in public, readable by people and agents.
record.score: The Composition is the score of the piece; the record is the score of the performance.

unlocks.how: the inputs (with checksums), every setting and the seed are enough to rebuild a performance exactly.
change one setting or swap one Supplier, and the new record shows exactly what changed.
Suppliers can see where their sounds were used. A usage view built from records is in draft for musicmatter.art.
performances of one Composition can be compared sound by sound and setting by setting.
the walk record traces every hop from the seed sound, drawn as a path chart.
agents can read, audit and build on any performance from the raw JSON.
records are unsigned for now. Signing is open decision #33.

record.notarism: Peter’s Notarism is about witnessing and recording existence. The record is NetComposer’s act of witness.

schema.status: draft format; fields may change; the walk record is the most complete example
schema.record_hash_rule: canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace) of the record without record_hash and signature

performances.title: The C major Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 846): take 5, forward/reverse echo
performances.settings: Chord strikes from musicmatter.art, two per bar. Each strike also plays reversed, swelling into the next. Hall 40%, 24 dB/oct low-pass swept 500 Hz → 20 kHz → 600 Hz.

performances.title: The C major Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 846): take 6 arps, 1/4 delay, hall 25%, LP 1 kHz
performances.settings: Up/down arpeggios from musicmatter.art, time-stretched to the half bar. 1/4 delay 40% fb, hall 25%, LP 1 kHz 24 dB/oct.

performances.title: The C major Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 846): search-driven take
performances.settings: Only the chords are fixed. Rhythm and figure contour come from the onsets of sounds the crawler found; notes, beds and bass are found sounds (no pitch-shift). Hall 30%.

performances.title: The C major Prelude, harmony only (after Bach, BWV 846): crawl walk
performances.settings: The timbre travels. Each bar's sounds were found by following links from the previous bar's: similar sounds, tags, packs, users, then out to Wikimedia Commons and the Internet Archive. Rhythm rotates with them. Only the chords are fixed. Hall 30%.

supplier_registry.crawl_policy: Registered Suppliers are listed in suppliers.json, where agents look first, and will be checked (licenses and checksums) on every validation run. Today the registry is checked with the validator. Beyond the registry, agents search the open commons (Freesound, Wikimedia Commons, Internet Archive); the NetComposer crawler is one tool for that.

create.what: Write a Composition in the browser, hear it with Play, then write Performance notes in the Perform section (editable immediately; Save, Undo, Cancel; Perform uses the current text) and press Perform for a hosted render. After it renders, the page shows the title, the player, Keep, and the dials. The signed record, sources, and JSON sit behind Record & sources. Keep holds the audio on the Performer past 90 days and does not list it. The player's own play control is the only one for that Performance, and the dials ride that same audio. Perform again replaces the result and hides the dials until the new render returns. Download composition.md and a plan stub, open a composition.md, share it as a link (the text rides in the URL hash; nothing is stored).

hosted_render.where: Inside Perform on /create/: Performance notes, then the Perform button, then progress, then the rendered result. The result shows the title, the player, the dials directly under that player, Keep, and Record & sources (closed). Perform again clears the player and the dials until the next render returns.
hosted_render.limits: 3 per 10 minutes, 10 per day, max_length_s 180, max_words 4000 characters

recordings.creator: Petrus
recordings.playback: the chosen instrument's default voicing from audio.musicmatter.art; a missing chord uses an alt voicing of that instrument, then piano, then a simple tone
recordings.sine: only when the instrument, its other voicings, and piano do not load; the page names the fallback

live.where: Directly under the hosted Performance player on /create/ (#live), hidden until a job is done, and hidden again when Perform again is pressed until the new render returns. The player is the only play control. Play higher on the page stays a plain preview of the Composition.
live.what: A human rides two hacks on the finished Performance while that player plays: low-pass and delay. Record keeps a WAV of that processed audio and a dial log that names the Performance (job id and audio sha). An uploaded dial log restores the moves when that Performance is still reachable.
live.runs: in the browser (Web Audio). The page player is the source (crossOrigin anonymous); the job file sends CORS *; nothing from Live is uploaded

hacks.lowpass: biquad lowpass, Q 0.707; cutoff 0..100, 0 = fully open, v -> 20000*(150/20000)^(v/100) Hz
hacks.delay: timing as a note value (1/16..1/2) at the Performance tempo, 60 BPM until the record names one; feedback 0..90%; wet/dry 0..100%, equal-power

take.audio: WAV, PCM 16-bit stereo, at the browser sample rate, of the processed Performance
take.dial_log: <performance-id>.live.dials.json, nc_live_log_version 0.3 (events timed in s from the start of the Performance audio; credits the Performance record, CC BY-SA 4.0)
